selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main lesson does the story try to teach about the daily prayers?
questions.answer: It teaches that the daily prayers are extremely valuable, easy to gain compared to their reward, and very foolish to neglect.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the one who neglects prayer is acting badly?
questions.answer: Because he gives up something very valuable even though it asks little from him.

questions.question: What happened when the first servant spent a little money in the right way?
questions.answer: It brought a huge increase in what he had.

questions.question: What transportation choices were available on the way?
questions.answer: There were land vehicles, a train, boats, and airplanes.

questions.question: What mistake did the other servant make besides wasting money?
questions.answer: He let entertainment distract him from his real mission.

questions.question: What kind of journey would the servant face if he ignored the advice?
questions.answer: He would face a long, lonely, hungry trip across harsh land.

questions.question: How much money did the careless servant have left at the end?
questions.answer: He had only one gold coin left.

questions.question: Why does the passage say even the least intelligent person can understand this point?
questions.answer: Because the right choice is very plain and does not require complicated thinking.

questions.question: What is the strongest message of the whole comparison?
questions.answer: A small effort for an important goal is wise, but neglecting that goal for passing pleasure is a serious mistake.

questions.question: What is the central message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Choosing brief sinful enjoyment over a small effort for a great reward is a reckless mistake.

questions.question: What idea is stressed at the very beginning of this passage about the prescribed prayers?
questions.answer: They are described as a central support of religion.

questions.question: What three ideas does the passage promise to explain through the comparison?
questions.answer: It explains the value of prayer, the small cost of gaining its reward, and the foolishness of neglecting it.

questions.question: What does sending them to a rich estate suggest about the destination?
questions.answer: It suggests the place was valuable and worth preparing for.

questions.question: What does the many transportation options show about the journey?
questions.answer: It shows that there were easier ways to arrive if a person used his money wisely.

questions.question: What made the second servant “luckless”?
questions.answer: He was lazy and wasted his money on useless pleasures.

questions.question: What was the friend trying to protect him from by telling him to buy the ticket?
questions.answer: He was trying to protect him from hardship, hunger, and a long difficult walk.

questions.question: What practical reason did the friend give for buying the ticket?
questions.answer: Without it, the journey would be long, exhausting, and hungry.

questions.question: What physical difficulties are named if he travels without the ticket?
questions.answer: He would have to walk a very long distance and suffer hunger.

questions.question: What kind of person is being warned in this comparison?
questions.answer: A person who ignores what truly matters and wastes his chances.

questions.question: What two things about the prescribed prayers does the passage especially want the reader to understand?
questions.answer: Their great worth and the serious foolishness of leaving them.

questions.question: Where were the two servants sent to go?
questions.answer: They were sent to settle on one of the ruler’s rich estates far away.

questions.question: What job were they expected to do after traveling?
questions.answer: They were expected to settle in and prepare a home on the ruler’s estate.

questions.question: How did the second servant’s choices hurt his future?
questions.answer: He used up almost everything for temporary fun and left himself unprepared.

questions.question: How did the fortunate servant use his money on the way to the station?
questions.answer: He spent only a small part of it and used some of it in a way that brought great profit.
